title: What Courtyard Cities Is
definition: Courtyard Cities: cities of shared courtyards instead of private yards.
description:
Courtyard Cities — Signature Edition: cities of shared courtyards instead of private yards. This is the JAH-original vision, designed from first principles and labeled as Signature speculation throughout.

The Signature court hulls program starts where public roadmaps stop. Where public research asks what is fundable, the Signature line asks what is buildable: shared districts rethought, walk transit rebuilt, communal kitchens reimagined for the century ahead. Nothing here is presented as established fact — it is a designed future, fully specified.

This edition mirrors the public database record for record — concept, components, milestones, demos, drills, alliance, roadmap — but every entry is the Signature take: bolder timelines, integrated systems thinking, and the arcade blocks ambition that defines the Signature line.

title: The Signature Vision: Courtyard Cities
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Courtyard Cities.
description:
The Signature vision of Courtyard Cities does not ask what committees will fund — it asks what physics allows and what engineering can compound.

Signature court hulls program, charter one: master shared districts at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale walk transit manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate communal kitchens systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

This is a Signature concept — original JAH speculation, fully specified and honestly labeled. The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Courtyard Cities becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

title: The court hulls Grid
definition: The court hulls Grid: a load-bearing component of Courtyard Cities.
description:
The urban backbone: power, water, data and logistics woven into one shared districts grid that the court hulls district runs on.

In the Courtyard Cities architecture, the court hulls grid is load-bearing: without it the court hulls fails outright — Courtyard Cities stops being Courtyard Cities at all. Builders sequence this piece early because every other component assumes it works. In the Signature architecture this piece is designed first-class, not bolted on.

Maturity varies: some deployments of this piece exist today in simpler forms, while the full Courtyard Cities-grade version remains a research target. The readiness estimator in this database scores it honestly.

t: 2030 — The first court hulls district opens at 50
title: 2030 — The first court hulls district opens at 50
definition: 2030 milestone on the Courtyard Cities roadmap.
description:
The first court hulls district opens at 50,000 residents, its shared districts grid and walk transit mobility running at full design load.

What must be true first: the shared districts results have to replicate outside the lab, walk transit manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and communal kitchens operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed shared districts demonstrations, walk transit cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting communal kitchens uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)
key_points: Target year: 2030 (4 years out).
Depends on: shared districts, walk transit, communal kitchens.

title: Readiness Estimator: Courtyard Cities
definition: Estimates Courtyard Cities readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Courtyard Cities components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a court hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Courtyard Cities Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Courtyard Cities operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Courtyard Cities installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 94066 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where shared districts monitoring, walk transit redundancy, or communal kitchens maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Courtyard Cities Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Courtyard Cities: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Courtyard Cities — cities of shared courtyards instead of private yards.

Phase 1 — Prove (shared districts): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (walk transit): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (communal kitchens): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (arcade blocks): court hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and old town-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
